can_answer: partly: annual recorded deaths per 1,000 reported crashes compare fatality counts relative to crash-record volume, but do not measure motorist or cyclist exposure or individual death risk
metric: Annual number of recorded motorist deaths and cyclist deaths per 1,000 police-reported crash rows, calculated as the relevant *_killed sum divided by the year's crash-row count and multiplied by 1,000
denominator: Count of all police-reported NYC motor vehicle crash rows in each calendar year (not people, trips, miles, or road-user exposure)
population: All police-reported NYC motor vehicle crash rows with crash_date in calendar years 2013 through 2025 inclusive; each death measure sums nonmissing values of its corresponding *_killed column
grouping: Calendar year, with two series: motorist deaths per 1,000 crashes and cyclist deaths per 1,000 crashes

data_check.population_rows_by_year: Recorded in check_2.csv; every year 2013–2025 has dates from January 1 through December 31.
data_check.filter_and_group_column: crash_date is a DATE, so empty strings and unknown words cannot occur as values; no rows have NULL dates, and no rows use 1900-01-01 or 1970-01-01 defaults. No impossible date values can be represented by the DATE type.
data_check.outcome_missing_rows: number_of_motorist_killed and number_of_cyclist_killed each have zero missing rows in every included year.

missing_data_decisions: Keep all in-range crash rows in each annual denominator and count their nonmissing killed-column values; no in-range rows are dropped or outcomes omitted due to missingness. All years are complete calendar years in the file.
plan_adjustment: No change to the initial framing; the check supports retaining all eligible rows and outcomes.
limitations: The rate is deaths per 1,000 police-reported crash rows, not per people, trips, miles, or motorist/cyclist exposure, and therefore is not an individual death-risk measure. It can change with crash-row volume as well as death counts.
